I like finding bullshit on GAF when the time is there and one of the more interesting threads of late is about the NX and something Miyamoto mentioned about it. There's no denying it's a safe haven for Nintendo fans, some of whom are unfortunately deluded, but one of the biggest offenders is Vena. I mean, read that carefully. Very carefully. Anyone who knows two shits about video game history knows they're pulling this out of their ass.

Now, if they'd just said the American home console industry would've probably not recovered after the crash, that'd be okay. Nintendo was fundamental in recovering it in America. But Europe never had a crash. Neither did Japan. The arcades and home computer markets didn't crash, either. And I'm not going to let them play their revisionists games. People tend to forget that the Master System did quite well in Europe and in fact the main reason it didn't in America was because of not just the NES, but Nintendo's stringent policies to 3rd parties. I'm not sure if Sega ever had something like the R.O.B at that time (that's the real reason NES was successful in America), but if their Genesis/Megadrive marketing is anything to go by, they'd of found a way to push Master System better in America. Besides, Mattel distributed it in the U.S afaik, and they'd of found ways to market it well as a toy.

Vena is another Nintendick (I say this only for the deluded Nintendo fans, not the reasonable ones) who thinks the entire industry revolves around their favorite console manufacturer. When at worst, without the NES the American market would have taken a couple extra years to recover at most, and Western devs would have likely focused more on PC for the time being before migrating efforts to systems like Master System and PC-Engine.

Speaking of which, there'd of been a 50/50 the PC-Engine did better in America, but none of that is supposing the SNES, which would've still released in America. MegaDrive/Genesis would have been more successful early on pre-Sonic, and that probably would have pushed SNES to release earlier, and things likely would have probably played out the same way in America as they did that gen with the only difference being a stronger PC-Engine/Turbographx.

I'm not knocking Nintendo's contribution to reviving the game industry. But, people need to realize that was an effort mostly concentrated in North America, and in the home console space. Other parts of the industry (computer, arcade) in other parts of the world (Japan, Europe) did just fine during those bleak times in the NA home console/arcade (well, arcades somewhat) market crash.

Anyhow, just wanted to share those thoughts.
